predecessors.name: Abbasid Caliphate
predecessors.text: the Abbasid province Arminiya, whose prince of princes (862) Ashot I was crowned king in 884 or 885

successors.name: Byzantine Empire
successors.text: Ani and the kingdom's remaining lands, surrendered by Catholicos Petros Getadardz in 1045

successors.name: Kingdom of Tashir-Dzoraget
successors.text: Tashir and Dzoraget, granted to Kiurike in 979 and independent after 1045

successors.name: Kingdom of Syunik
successors.text: Syunik, independent since 987 under Bagratid overlordship

successors.name: Armenian Kingdom of Cilicia
successors.text: listed as a successor in the infobox

successors.name: Kingdom of Kars
successors.text: Kars (Vanand), whose king received the Bagratuni title 'King of Kings' after 1045 and ceded the kingdom to Byzantium in 1065

ledger.x: 885: Ashot I is crowned king of Armenia.
Late 9th century: Syunik under the Bagratid kings.
890: the capital moves from Bagaran to Shirakavan (infobox: Bagaran 885-890, Shirakavan 890-929).
April 892: Smbat I retakes Dvin.
902: Smbat I grants Nakhchavan to Ashot Artsruni.
903: Smbat I annexes Abkhazian districts.
904: Smbat I takes Nakhchavan back.
908: Vaspurakan leaves under its own king.
909: Yusuf of Azerbaijan invades Armenia.
909: Yusuf takes Nakhichevan.

c. 911: the Ardahan annexation lapses. No page gives an end: the Smbat I page does not say the Abkhazian districts were lost or retaken. Smbat was beaten at Dzknavachar in 910 and surrendered in 914, and Cliopatria's 911 shape (56,711 km2) contains none of Ardahan, so the end is bridged to 911. Bridging.
914: Smbat I surrenders and is killed.
929: the capital moves from Shirakavan to Kars (infobox: Kars 929-961).
961: Ashot III relocates the capital from Kars to Ani, the year of his investiture as king.
963: Mushegh I founds the Kingdom of Kars (Vanand) as a Bagratid sub-kingdom.
979: Tashir is granted to Kiurike as a vassal kingdom.
987: Syunik declares itself a separate kingdom.
988: Syunik again recognises the Bagratid king.
989-1020: Gagik I takes Vayots Dzor from Syunik.
1001: the western strip toward Tayk goes to Byzantium.
1021: the kingdom divides between the brothers Hovhannes-Smbat III and Ashot IV.
1022: Fadl I takes Dvin.
1045: Kiurike II becomes independent of the fallen Bagratids.
1045: the Bagratid overlordship of Syunik ends with the kingdom.
1045: with Ani surrendered, Kars no longer answers to a Bagratid king of Ani.
1045: Ani passes to Byzantium.

wars.name: Sajid campaigns against Armenia
wars.outcome: Yusuf captured Dvin in 901 (retaken by Smbat), crowned Gagik Artsruni in 908, invaded in 909, beat Smbat at Dzknavachar in 910 and had him beheaded in 914; Vaspurakan leaves the kingdom.

wars.name: Abkhazian invasion of 943
wars.outcome: An 'invasion by king Ber of Abkhazia in 943'; no land change is recorded.

wars.name: Battle of Tsumb
wars.outcome: 'whose armies defeated Mamlan, the emir of Khorasan, in 998 in the village of Tsumb, northeast of Lake Van': the sentence follows Gagik I's alliance with Bagrat III and Gurgen of Iberia, whose armies are meant.

wars.name: Byzantine invasions of Ani
wars.outcome: 'In 1044, the Byzantines twice invaded Ani but failed to conquer it'; in 1045 Catholicos Petros Getadardz surrendered Ani to the Byzantines.

certainty.note: No page gives a boundary or area for any year; the kingdom was a loose overlordship of princes (Syunik, Tashir-Dzoraget, Vaspurakan) and the shape mixes direct land and suzerainty.
